title: Article 6 High-Risk AI Classification Rules
content: AI systems used as safety components in products or systems falling under EU harmonization legislation (Annex I) and systems listed in Annex III are classified as high-risk. Annex III covers biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, access to essential services, law enforcement, migration, and administration of justice.

title: Article 9 Risk Management System for High-Risk AI
content: A continuous iterative risk management system must be established and maintained throughout the entire lifecycle of high-risk AI systems. It requires systematic identification of foreseeable risks, adoption of targeted mitigation measures, and post-market empirical stress testing.

title: Article 10 Data and Data Governance Quality Criteria
content: Training, validation, and testing datasets must be subject to rigorous data governance practices. Datasets must be relevant, representative, free of systematic statistical errors, and complete in view of the intended purpose, with specific measures to detect and mitigate demographic biases.

title: Article 11 Technical Documentation and Record-Keeping
content: Technical documentation must be drawn up before the system is placed on the market and kept up to date. Documentation must demonstrate compliance with Chapter III requirements and provide national competent authorities with clear audit trails including model architecture, algorithmic design, and data provenance.

title: Article 13 Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
content: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret the system output and use it appropriately. Systems must be accompanied by comprehensive instructions for use in digital format.

title: Article 14 Human Oversight Design Requirements
content: High-risk AI systems must be designed to enable natural persons to oversee their operation, understand capacities and limitations, monitor for anomalies, and exercise real-time override or operational stop mechanisms without fear of automated retribution.

title: Article 15 Accuracy, Robustness, and Cybersecurity
content: Systems must achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, maintaining resilience against adversarial attacks, data poisoning, prompt injection, model extraction, and unintended runtime edge-case drifts.

title: Article 17 Right to Erasure and Machine Unlearning
content: Data subjects retain the absolute right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data without undue delay. For enterprise AI deployments, fine-tuned model checkpoints and vector embedding stores must implement certified machine unlearning and cryptographic index deletion procedures.

title: Chapter V International Transfers and Sovereign Boundary Enforcement
content: Personal data transfers outside the European Economic Area (EEA) require Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or adequacy decisions. Cloud deployments in Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and Netherlands (europe-west4) maintain sovereign zero-egress posture ensuring full data residency compliance.

title: Weaviate Isolated Multi-Tenant Memory Architecture
content: Enterprise vector stores require hard multi-tenancy where customer namespaces are partitioned at the shard level. Embedding vectors are encrypted at rest with customer-managed AWS KMS or GCP Cloud KMS keys, preventing cross-tenant semantic data leakage during similarity search.

title: Claude Prompt Caching Latency and Cost Mechanics
content: Prompt caching allows reusable conversational prefixes, system instructions, and vector-retrieved enterprise policies to be cached in Anthropic KV-cache memory with a 5-minute rolling TTL. Cached input tokens achieve 90% cost savings and up to 80% latency reduction for high-throughput multi-turn agents.

title: Polars SIMD Columnar Ingestion Pipeline
content: Polars leverages Apache Arrow memory and Rust multi-threading to execute vector preparation pipelines 15x faster than legacy Pandas. Streaming lazy execution prevents out-of-memory errors on massive enterprise corpora during tokenization and metadata extraction.
